title: Module breaking-change safety and migration playbook — private deployments
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic playbook for making and rolling out breaking changes to Terraform modules used by Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) customers. It codifies how we classify compatibility changes, the guardrails engineers must follow before merging a breaking change, and the operational rollout/migration steps to minimize customer impact.

Scope:
- Applies to all internal Terraform modules under terraform-modules/* that are consumed by private deployments (VPC, on-prem installers, bootstrap manifests).
- Covers semantic versioning policy, compatibility classification, change review checklist, CI/automation requirements, publishing to our internal module index, migration guide template, and rollback procedures.
- Does NOT cover infra-level manual changes (host OS patches, network reconfigs) except where they are surfaced as module inputs/outputs.

Quick rules (TL;DR):
- Any API change that removes or renames module inputs/outputs or changes resource addresses => breaking change. Bump MAJOR version.
- Additive inputs/outputs or safe defaults => MINOR or PATCH.
- If in doubt, add a new version line and keep the old behaviour for one release cycle.

Versioning policy (concrete):
- We follow strict semver for modules: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Module consumers must pin to major version (e.g., 2.x) in release manifests for private deployments.
- Major bump allowed only after the breaking-change checklist is satisfied and a cross-team review is completed.
- Deprecation period: When we remove or rename an input/output we must provide at least one major release cycle where both old and new inputs are accepted (via aliased inputs or wrapper variables) before removing entirely.

Breaking-change classification and examples:
- Class 1 (Hard break): Rename or remove variable, output, or resource address used by consumers. Example: changing variable name var.subnet_ids -> var.private_subnet_ids.
- Class 2 (Behavioral break): Change default behavior that affects provisioning (e.g., enable a feature flag default to true when previously false) without opt-in.
- Class 3 (Performance/scale break): Changes that can cause resource churn (different lifecycle behavior) at scale.

Pre-merge checklist (must be completed before merging a PR that causes MAJOR bump):
- [ ] Author writes compatibility summary in PR description describing what changes and why.
- [ ] Compatibility matrix updated: list of module consumers (pipelines, on-prem installers, customer manifests) and the required migration action for each.
- [ ] Migration guide draft attached to PR (see template below).
- [ ] Automated compatibility test(s) added to module CI: run a set of pinned consumer configs against both old and new versions (terraform plan only in CI).
- [ ] Static checks: tflint, tfsec, and a custom tf-schema validator pass.
- [ ] Security review sign-off if change touches IAM, secrets, or network defaults.
- [ ] Docs updated: module README and CHANGELOG (explicitly mark breaking items).
- [ ] Package build: confirm module archive artifact and checksums generated by CI.
- [ ] Release owner assigned and release window scheduled (include on-call SRE).

Publishing steps to internal index (high level):
- Prepare release branch: release/<module-name>/vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.
- CI builds module package: tar.gz + SHA256, runs acceptance tests (see note below).
- Tag repo with semver tag vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.
- Push artifact to internal module index (private-mod-index.redwood.internal) via release pipeline. The pipeline registers the new version in the index metadata.
- Create release notes entry in internal releases doc and update the module README with migration link.

Automated tests and CI requirements:
- Unit: tflint, tfsec, terraform validate (with 1.6+ installed).
- Integration: run terraform init/plan against a small set of consumer root modules (stored under tests/consumers/) pinned to the previous major; expect plan to either be empty or contain explicit migrations outlined in the migration guide.
- Acceptance (optional for patch/minor): ephemeral apply in isolated GCP/AZURE sandbox to detect resource drift. For major breaks, acceptance must include a full apply/plan cycle and rollback smoke test.

Migration guide template (include in PR):
- Summary of change (2–3 bullets).
- Affected consumers: list repos/pipelines and contact owners.
- Migration steps (exact terraform changes) with example snippets.
- Estimated effort and risk (low/medium/high).
- Rollback steps and how to pin to older major if needed.

Sample migration snippet (to include in guide):
- Before (root module using older module):
  module "network" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//network?ref=v1.3.2"
    subnet_ids = var.subnet_ids
  }

- After (consumer changes to new major):
  module "network" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//network?ref=v2.0.0"
    private_subnet_ids = var.subnet_ids # mapping wrapper to keep backwards compatibility during transition
  }

Rollout plan for private/on-prem customers:
- Canary cohort: select up to 3 internal staging clusters or pilot customer manifests to upgrade first. Run the full installer and smoke tests.
- Monitoring window: 72 hours after canary upgrade with SLO/alerting on provisioning errors, resource diffs, and any post-provisioning health checks.
- Gradual ramp: if canary stable, ramp to next wave of customers (batch size configurable).
- For on-prem managed installs: coordinate with Professional Services/SE to schedule upgrades, communicate downtime or manual steps, and open a post-upgrade support channel.

Rollback strategy:
- Consumers must be able to pin module major versions. If a regression is detected, instruct customers to pin to previous major (e.g., 1.x) and redeploy.
- For stateful resource renames, provide a state migration helper script (terraform state mv commands) and document pre-checks.
- In extreme cases, release a quickfix major that preserves both behaviours via compatibility shims, then iterate with a minor/patch to remove shims later.

Changelog and communication templates:
- Changelog entry format: date | vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH | [BREAKING] short summary — owner initials — migration link.
- Customer email template (for on-prem managed customers): short description, impact, required action, rollback instructions, support contact, scheduled windows.

Maintenance and deprecation cadence:
- After publishing a major that deprecates inputs/outputs, add an item to the module TODO board to remove shims after 6 months or after two major cycles, whichever is longer.
- Track deprecation TTL per module in the module metadata file (module-meta.yaml).

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Module owners: author team that maintains the module and triages consumer issues. Must be assigned at PR time.
- Release owner: responsible for coordinating the rollout, owning the release window and post-release monitoring.
- SRE on-call: must be looped for major releases for private deployments.

Open questions / edge cases (to discuss in weekly eng-private-deploy sync):
- Should we automate a consumer impact scan (static analysis to detect variable/output usage across all infra repos) before accepting a breaking PR? Proposal: run grep + TF parser across monorepo and generate a consumer list. (RDW-1987)
- How to support air-gapped customers for artifact distribution? We currently support tarball downloads — need documented steps for PS to deliver and validate.
- What visibility do we provide to customers for module deprecation schedules? UX/console item to show upcoming breaking changes?

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- Pin a module in a consumer: source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//<module>?ref=v1.4.0"
- Terraform plan against pinned module: TF_IN_AUTOMATION=1 terraform init -backend=false && terraform plan
- Example tf-schema aliasing pattern for compatibility (in variables.tf):
  variable "private_subnet_ids" { type = list(string) }
  variable "subnet_ids" { type = list(string) default = null }
  locals { merged_subnet_ids = coalesce(var.private_subnet_ids, var.subnet_ids) }

Next steps (action items):
- Review this playbook in eng-private-deploy meeting (owner: Samir) — target: 2026-03-10.
- Implement consumer-impact scanner prototype (owner: Joanna) — target: 2026-04-01.
- Add a CI job template for major-release acceptance tests in our shared-ci (owner: Elias) — target: 2026-03-20.

Notes to reviewers:
- This document is intentionally pragmatic — aimed at reducing unplanned customer work while allowing the team to iterate on module APIs. Expect follow-ups to refine automation and the artifact distribution story for air-gapped customers.
- If you are a module consumer, please read the Migration guide template and verify your repo's pinning policy.
